title: Transitions to super-radiance in ensembles of incoherently pumped emitters
abstract: Super-radiance is a striking phenomenon resulting from the collective interaction of emitters with light, and it is fundamentally related to the appearance of long-range correlations between the dipole moments of the emitters. As such, it represents a distinct phase of dissipative many-body systems compared to the case of independent emitters, similarly to how ferromagnetism stands out in magnetic materials in contrast to paramagnetism. In this work we address the conditions under which the transition to super-radiance can occur in ensembles of emitters subject to dephasing and individual decay -- a situation which is particularly relevant to the case of emitters in the solid state. The simplifying assumption of an ensemble of permutationally invariant emitters allows for the efficient solution of both the dissipative dynamics after a pulsed excitation, as well as of the steady state under incoherent pumping. This exact solution allows us to benchmark a truncated cumulant expansion approach, which can give predictions for arbitrarily big system sizes. We show that super-radiance is fundamentally robust to sizable dephasing and non-radiative decay rates, both under a pulsed excitation, as well as under continuous pumping. This robustness is the result of the collective acceleration effect of super-radiant emission with respect to the individual coupling to a local environment. We establish the universal critical scaling laws at the transition between normal radiance and super-radiance; and we show that, in the super-radiant phase, significant finite-size crossovers can be observed before reaching the asymptotic scaling regime. Our results pave the way for future experiments to provide a quantitative characterization of the scaling properties of super-radiance, seen as a distinct non-equilibrium many-body phase in ensembles of incoherently pumped emitters.
summary: The paper rigorously analyzes the super-radiant transition in ensembles of emitters facing environmental noise. By using exact solutions and cumulant expansions, it establishes that collective emission remains robust to dephasing but faces limitations from individual decay rates. This work provides quantitative scaling laws for this non-equilibrium many-body phase relevant for solid-state quantum optics.
main_problem: The work investigates the conditions under which super-radiance, a collective quantum emission phenomenon, can occur in ensembles of emitters subjected to environmental decoherence mechanisms like dephasing and individual decay.
main_result: Super-radiance is shown to be fundamentally robust against sizable dephasing rates, particularly when considering fixed coupling regimes; however, individual decay introduces critical size limitations for observing asymptotic scaling.
method: The authors employ an exact solution exploiting permutational invariance for small systems and benchmark this against a truncated cumulant expansion approach for larger sizes.
model_or_system: The system models ensembles of identical emitters coupled to a common light mode, described by dynamics governed by a Lindblad master equation incorporating pumping, collective emission, individual decay, and dephasing terms.
key_observables: Average values of collective spin operators ($\langle J_z angle$, $\langle J^+J^- angle$), super-radiant emission intensity scaling, and Quantum Fisher Information (QFI).
important_parameters: Dephasing rate ($\gamma_\phi$), individual decay rate ($\gamma_d$), system size ($N$), and the coupling scheme (fixed density vs. fixed coupling).
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is the permutational invariance of the emitters, which allows for simplification into collective spin variables.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the scaling of collective emission rates under different coupling schemes and show time evolution trajectories in the Dicke manifold $(J, M)$ plane, alongside the evolution of quantum coherence measures like QFI during super-radiant bursts.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the dynamics by first establishing the theoretical framework using master equations, then solving it exactly for small $N$, extending to large $N$ via cumulant expansions, and finally comparing the robustness of super-radiance under different environmental couplings (dephasing vs. decay).
why_interesting: This work provides crucial quantitative insights into non-equilibrium many-body physics, specifically characterizing a distinct dissipative phase transition (super-radiance) in realistic solid-state environments where decoherence is unavoidable.

Figure 2: Steady-state phase diagrams within the two coupling schemes of the emit- ters to the common emission mode: (a) fixed-density scheme; (b) fixed-coupling scheme.

Figure 3: Steady-state phase diagram in the pumping vs. dephasing plane (a), and in the pumping vs. individual decay plane (b). The phases are characterized by the order parameter 〈J+J−〉/N 2 obtained with the TCE1 approximation. The grey dashed line is the critical line given in Eq. (14)).

Figure 4: Steady-state phase transition from super-radiance to normal emission upon increasing the pumping rate rp: (a) 〈Jz〉/N related to the average density of excited emitters; (b) integrated, normalized dipole-dipole correlations 〈J+J−〉/N 2, (c) von- Neumann entropy per emitter S(ρ)/N = −Tr(ρ lnρ)/N and (d) quantum Fisher information density for the operator J x. All solid lines correspond to exact results. The black dashed lines correspond to TCE1 predictions, Eqs. (11) and (15), and are independent of N.
